---
title: "Several contents on one page"
description: >
  A table under a table, a figure under a table, and a long listing that
  goes on over pages of its own: the
  arguments that place them, the titles and footnotes, the sections and the
  page values, and rtf_layout() to check the pages before writing them.
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
# A chunk's code sits under "Show code": open when it is what the page is
# about (`fold = "open"`), closed when it only supports it (`fold = "closed"`,
# the default unless the page sets another); `fold = FALSE` shows it plain,
# and so is code of three lines or fewer.
# Its results stay outside, always shown.
.fold_src <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("source")
knitr::knit_hooks$set(source = function(x, options) {
  f <- if (is.null(options$fold)) "closed" else options$fold
  if (isFALSE(f) || length(unlist(strsplit(x, "\n", fixed = TRUE))) <= 3L) {
    return(.fold_src(x, options))
  }
  paste0("\n\n<details", if (identical(f, "open")) " open", ">",
         "<summary>Show code</summary>\n\n",
         .fold_src(x, options), "\n\n</details>\n\n")
})
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fold = "open")   # this page: the code is the subject
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
                      message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
options(width = 100)
# The files are written in a folder of their own: RTFREPORTER_ARTICLE_OUT
# when data-raw/gen_several_contents.R renders the page (it makes the
# pictures from them), a temporary one otherwise.  The pictures are
# committed in img/several-contents/ beside this page, so they show on
# GitHub too.
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = Sys.getenv("RTFREPORTER_ARTICLE_OUT", tempdir()))
```

<p align="right">
  <a class="btn btn-outline-secondary btn-sm" href="several-contents-ja.html">In Japanese</a>
</p>

A report often puts two contents on one page: a summary table and the
listing behind it, a table and its figure, two short tables. In rtfreporter
each `rtf_tables()` or `rtf_figures()` call adds a content, and
`page_break = FALSE` puts it under the content before it instead of on a new
page. This page shows three such reports and the rules behind them.

```{r setup, fold = FALSE}
library(rtfreporter)
```

## The arguments

| Argument | Of | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `page_break` | `rtf_tables()`, `rtf_figures()` | `TRUE` (the default): the content starts a page. `FALSE`: it goes on under the content before it. |
| `space_before` | both | With `page_break = FALSE`, the empty lines between the two. |
| `titles`, `footnotes` | both | The content's own title block (above it) and footnote block (under it). |
| `first_rows` | `rtf_tables()` | With `page_break = FALSE`, the rows of the table that go on the shared page. The rest is paginated as the table says (a plan's `plan_paginate_rows()`), each page with its title, column header and footnote. |
| `cont_title` | `rtf_tables()` | With `first_rows`, a line under the title of each later page, such as `"(continued)"`. |

The header and footer of the page (`rtf_section(header = , footer = )`) are
the page's, not a content's: they print on every page whatever is on it.

**Fitting the page is the program's job.** rtfreporter does not measure the
page. A content that does not fit is carried to the next page by the reader
(Word, LibreOffice), with no title, column header or footnote there, and the
page numbers written into the file (`{PAGE}` / `{TOTAL_PAGES}`) are then
off. Count what fits: make the first content short enough, give a figure its
height, and give a long table `first_rows`. `rtf_layout()`, at the end of
this page, shows the pages as rtfreporter will write them.

## (a) A table under a table

An overview of the treatment-emergent adverse events and, under it, the
demographic characteristics of the same population: two ARDs and two plans,
with one column header -- the arm and its N -- written once and used by
both.

```{r a-data, fold = "closed"}
arms <- c("Placebo", "Xanomeline Low Dose", "Xanomeline High Dose")
adsl <- cards::ADSL[cards::ADSL$SAFFL == "Y", ]
adsl$ARM <- factor(adsl$ARM, levels = arms)
adae <- cards::ADAE[cards::ADAE$TRTEMFL == "Y", ]
# a subject-level flag for each row of the overview
had <- function(rows) adsl$USUBJID %in% adae$USUBJID[rows]
adsl$ANYAE <- had(TRUE)
adsl$RELAE <- had(adae$AEREL %in% c("POSSIBLE", "PROBABLE"))
adsl$SEVAE <- had(adae$AESEV == "SEVERE")
adsl$SERAE <- had(adae$AESER == "Y")
adsl$DISAE <- adsl$DSRAEFL %in% "Y"
adsl$DTHAE <- had(adae$AESDTH == "Y")
ard_ae <- cards::ard_tabulate_value(adsl, by = ARM,
                                    variables = c(ANYAE, RELAE, SEVAE, SERAE, DISAE, DTHAE))
ard_dm <- cards::ard_stack(
  adsl, .by = ARM,
  cards::ard_summary(variables = AGE),
  cards::ard_tabulate(variables = c(AGEGR1, SEX, RACE)))

# the column header both tables share: the arm and its N
arm_header <- rtf_col_header(c("", "{col}"), c("", "(N={n})"))
ae <- ard_ae |>
  normalize_ard() |>
  table_plan(cols = "ARM", rows = "variable") |>
  plan_cells(c(n == 0 ~ "0", "{n:.0f} ({p:.1f%})"), notes = FALSE) |>
  plan_labels(c(ANYAE = "Any TEAE", RELAE = "Any drug-related TEAE",
                SEVAE = "Any severe TEAE", SERAE = "Any serious TEAE",
                DISAE = "Any TEAE leading to discontinuation",
                DTHAE = "Any TEAE leading to death")) |>
  plan_col_header(values = list(n = TRUE), arm_header) |>
  plan_hide("label") |>
  plan_columns(widths = c(4, 2, 2, 2)) |>
  plan_style(border = "tfl", align_count_pct = TRUE)
dm <- ard_dm |>
  normalize_ard() |>
  table_plan(cols = "ARM", rows = c(group = "variable")) |>
  plan_cells(continuous = c("n" = "{N:.0f}", "Mean (SD)" = "{mean:.1f} ({sd:.2f})",
                            "Median" = "{median:.1f}", "Min, Max" = "{min:.0f}, {max:.0f}"),
             categorical = c(n == 0 ~ "0", "{n:.0f} ({p:.1f%})"), notes = FALSE) |>
  plan_labels(c(AGE = "Age (years)", AGEGR1 = "Age group (years), n (%)",
                SEX = "Sex, n (%)", RACE = "Race, n (%)")) |>
  plan_levels(AGEGR1 = c("<65", "65-80", ">80"), SEX = c("F", "M")) |>
  plan_col_header(values = list(n = TRUE), arm_header) |>
  plan_stub(name = "row_label") |>
  plan_columns(widths = c(4, 2, 2, 2)) |>
  plan_style(border = "tfl", align_count_pct = TRUE)
```

The first `rtf_tables()` starts the page; the second, with
`page_break = FALSE`, goes on under it, one empty line between them:

```{r a-doc}
header <- rtf_header(list(c(l = "Protocol: CDISCPILOT01", r = "Page {PAGE} of {TOTAL_PAGES}")))
doc_a <- rtf_document() |>
  rtf_section(header = header) |>
  rtf_tables(ae, titles = list(c("Table 14.3.1.1",
                                 "Overview of Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events and Demographic Characteristics",
                                 "Safety Population")),
             footnotes = list(c("TEAE = treatment-emergent adverse event. A subject is counted once in each row.",
                                "Drug-related: possibly or probably related to the study drug, as judged by the investigator."))) |>
  rtf_tables(dm, page_break = FALSE, space_before = 1L,
             titles = list("Demographic Characteristics"),
             footnotes = list("Percentages are based on the number of subjects in the Safety Population in each arm."))
generate_rtfreport(doc_a, "a_table_table.rtf", overwrite = TRUE)
```

![The overview of adverse events with the demographic characteristics under it on one page](img/several-contents/a_table_table.png)

Each table keeps its own title and footnote. The output's own title (the
table number, its name and the population) is the first content's title
block; a footnote for the whole output is the last content's footnote block,
or the page footer when it is wanted on every page.

## (b) A figure under a table

A Kaplan-Meier plot under its table: the events, the censored subjects, the
median time with its confidence interval, and the number at risk at the
plot's ticks. The table is a plain data frame, made from the `survfit()`
fit the plot draws:

```{r b-data, fold = "closed"}
adtte <- cards::ADTTE[cards::ADTTE$PARAMCD == "TTDE", ]
adtte$TRTA <- factor(adtte$TRTA, levels = arms)
fit <- survival::survfit(survival::Surv(AVAL, 1 - CNSR) ~ TRTA, data = adtte)
s <- summary(fit)$table
q <- quantile(fit, probs = 0.5)
ne <- function(x) if (is.na(x)) "NE" else format(round(x))
days <- c(0, 28, 56, 84, 112, 140, 168)
at_risk <- matrix(summary(fit, times = days, extend = TRUE)$n.risk, ncol = length(arms))
km_tab <- data.frame(
  Item = c("Subjects with an event, n (%)", "Censored, n (%)",
           "Median time to event (days) (95% CI)", "Number at risk", paste0("  Day ", days)))
for (i in seq_along(arms)) {
  n <- s[i, "records"]
  e <- s[i, "events"]
  km_tab[[arms[i]]] <- c(sprintf("%d (%.1f)", e, 100 * e / n),
                         sprintf("%d (%.1f)", n - e, 100 * (n - e) / n),
                         sprintf("%s (%s, %s)", ne(q$quantile[i]), ne(q$lower[i]), ne(q$upper[i])),
                         "", as.character(at_risk[, i]))
}
names(km_tab)[1] <- ""
km_table <- table_plan(km_tab) |>
  plan_col_header(rtf_col_header(c("", arms), c("", sprintf("(N=%d)", s[, "records"])))) |>
  plan_columns(widths = c(4, 2, 2, 2)) |>
  plan_style(border = "tfl")
```

`rtf_figures()` takes the same `page_break` and `space_before`. Give the
figure the height that is left on the page:

```{r b-doc}
library(ggplot2)
# the curves from `fit` above: a step from (0, 1) per arm, a + at each censoring
arm <- sub("^TRTA=", "", names(fit$strata))
km_df <- rbind(data.frame(time = 0, surv = 1, arm = arm, n.censor = 0),
               data.frame(time = fit$time, surv = fit$surv,
                          arm = rep(arm, fit$strata), n.censor = fit$n.censor))
km_plot <- ggplot(km_df, aes(time, surv, colour = arm)) +
  geom_step(linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(data = km_df[km_df$n.censor > 0, ], shape = 3, size = 1.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = days) +
  labs(x = "Days since first dose", y = "Probability of no dermatologic event") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 9) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.title = element_blank())
doc_b <- rtf_document() |>
  rtf_section(header = header) |>
  rtf_tables(km_table, titles = list(c("Figure 14.3.2.1",
                                       "Kaplan-Meier Plot of Time to First Dermatologic Event",
                                       "Safety Population"))) |>
  rtf_figures(km_plot, page_break = FALSE, space_before = 1L,
              render_width = 7, render_height = 3.2,
              footnotes = list(c("Dermatologic event: a treatment-emergent skin and subcutaneous tissue event.",
                                 "+ Censored at the last contact.",
                                 "Median and 95% CI from the Kaplan-Meier estimate. NE = not estimable.")))
generate_rtfreport(doc_b, "b_table_figure.rtf", overwrite = TRUE)
```

![The time-to-event table with the Kaplan-Meier plot under it](img/several-contents/b_table_figure.png)

## (c) A long listing that goes on

A disposition summary and, under it, the listing of the subjects who
discontinued: 144 subjects, far more than what is left under the summary.
The listing is a plain table, its columns as they print, named as their
headers. `plan_row_group()` prints the treatment on its first row only (and
again at the top of a page), and `plan_paginate_rows()` makes pages of 30
rows:

```{r d-listing}
ard_ds <- cards::ard_stack(adsl, .by = ARM, cards::ard_tabulate(variables = DCDECOD))
ds <- ard_ds |>
  normalize_ard() |>
  table_plan(cols = "ARM", rows = c(group = "variable")) |>
  plan_cells(categorical = c(n == 0 ~ "0", "{n:.0f} ({p:.1f%})"), notes = FALSE) |>
  plan_labels(c(DCDECOD = "Status at end of study, n (%)")) |>
  plan_col_header(values = list(n = TRUE), arm_header) |>
  plan_stub(name = "row_label") |>
  plan_columns(widths = c(4, 2, 2, 2)) |>
  plan_style(border = "tfl", align_count_pct = TRUE)

disc <- adsl[adsl$DCDECOD != "COMPLETED", ]
disc <- disc[order(disc$ARM, disc$USUBJID), ]
lst <- data.frame(Treatment = as.character(disc$ARM),
                  `Subject ID` = disc$USUBJID,
                  `Age/Sex` = paste0(disc$AGE, "/", disc$SEX),
                  `Last dose (study day)` = as.character(disc$TRTDUR),
                  `Reason for discontinuation` = tools::toTitleCase(tolower(disc$DCDECOD)),
                  check.names = FALSE)
disc_listing <- table_plan(lst) |>
  plan_row_group(mode = "value", collapse = "Treatment", group_col = "Treatment") |>
  plan_paginate_rows(max_rows = 30, split = "group_force") |>
  plan_columns(widths = c(2.4, 1.6, 1, 1.6, 3)) |>
  plan_style(border = "tfl")
```

(`plan_listing()` and `listing_spec()` are for listings whose records wrap
over several lines, such as adverse events. See
[Listings with a plan](plan-listings.html). A listing whose summary shares its
columns -- a PK concentration listing with its summary statistics under it --
is one table, not two contents: see
[A listing and its summary in one table](plan-append.html).)

`first_rows` says how many of the listing's rows go on the shared page; the
rest goes on pages of its own, paginated by its plan, each with the
listing's title, the `cont_title` line, the column header and the footnote:

```{r d-doc}
doc_d <- rtf_document() |>
  rtf_section(header = header) |>
  rtf_tables(ds, titles = list(c("Table 14.1.2",
                                 "Subject Disposition and Subjects Who Discontinued",
                                 "Safety Population"))) |>
  rtf_tables(disc_listing, page_break = FALSE, space_before = 1L,
             first_rows = 12L, cont_title = "(continued)",
             titles = list("Subjects Who Discontinued the Study"),
             footnotes = list("Last dose: the study day of the last dose, day 1 being the first."))
generate_rtfreport(doc_d, "c_listing.rtf", overwrite = TRUE)
```

Page 1, the summary and the first 12 rows of the listing:

![Page 1: the disposition summary and the first rows of the listing](img/several-contents/c_listing_page1.png)

Page 2, where the listing goes on:

![Page 2: the listing continued, titled (continued)](img/several-contents/c_listing_page2.png)

A footnote given to `rtf_tables(footnotes = )` belongs to that content and
prints under it, on each of its pages; one wanted on every page goes in the
page footer.

## Checking the pages: `rtf_layout()`

`rtf_layout()` lays the document out as `generate_rtfreport()` will write
it, without writing it: one line per content on each page, with the rows of
each table and the size of each figure. Use it to count what goes on a page
and to see where a content is cut:

```{r layout}
rtf_layout(doc_d)
```

The result is a list as well: `rtf_layout(doc)$pages` has one entry per
printed page, each with its `segments` (the contents on it, top to bottom).

## Sections on a page of several contents

`rtf_tables(auto_section = TRUE)` opens a section for each named content, so
each can have its own header and footer values. A page has one header and
one footer, so a page of several contents has one section:

* the page takes the section of the **first content on it that has one**;
* a later content on the page with a different one gets a warning, and its
  section is not used: no page break is added for it;
* a page whose contents have none stays in the section before it.

```{r sections}
df <- function(n) data.frame(Item = sprintf("Row %02d", seq_len(n)), N = seq_len(n))
doc_s <- rtf_document() |>
  rtf_tables(list(Overview = df(3)), titles = "Table 1") |>
  rtf_tables(list("Part B" = df(4)), titles = "Table 2", auto_section = TRUE,
             page_break = FALSE)
rtf_layout(doc_s)
```

The first table has no section, so the page takes "Part B" from the second.
Page breaks come only from `page_break` and the tables' own pagination.

## A page's values in titles and headers: `{column}`

A table cut into pages on a column -- `as_rtftables(page_by = )`, a plan's
`plan_paginate_group()` -- knows each page's value of that column. A title,
footnote, header or footer writes `{<column name>}` and gets that value:

```{r tokens}
lab <- data.frame(PARAM = rep(c("ALT (U/L)", "AST (U/L)"), each = 3),
                  Visit = rep(c("Baseline", "Week 2", "Week 4"), 2),
                  Mean  = c(21.3, 22.0, 21.8, 24.1, 24.9, 25.2))
pages <- as_rtftables(lab, page_by = "PARAM", drop_cols = "PARAM")
doc_t <- rtf_document() |>
  rtf_section(header = rtf_header(list(c(l = "Parameter: {PARAM}",
                                         r = "Page {PAGE} of {TOTAL_PAGES}")))) |>
  rtf_tables(pages, titles = list(c("Table 14.3.1", "Mean of {PARAM} by Visit")))
rtf_layout(doc_t)
rtf_layout(doc_t)$pages[[2]]$values     # the values of page 2
generate_rtfreport(doc_t, "t_tokens.rtf", overwrite = TRUE)
```

![Page 2 of the lab table, its header and title naming AST](img/several-contents/t_tokens_page2.png)

On a page of several contents, a title or footnote takes the value of its
own table, so each names its own. The header and footer belong to the page:
each column takes the value of the first table on the page that has one,
and a later table with another value gets a warning (the rule of the
sections above). A `{NAME}` the page has no value for prints as written;
rtfreporter's own tokens (`{PAGE}`, `{PROGRAM}`, ...) and those given to
`rtf_document(tokens = )` win over a column of the same name.
